S_storage.definition: S(r) = |r| bits. Memory to store representation r.

W_work.definition: W(r) = total gate count to evaluate r. = circuit size C(r).

T_time.definition: T(r, p) = wall-clock steps on p processors = ⌈W(r)/p⌉ + overhead.
T_time.counterexample: Parallel decomposition: f=g∘h, W same, T halved. [MEASURED]

D_depth.definition: D(r) = longest path in execution DAG (critical path).
D_depth.counterexample: Sequential XOR depth=d vs balanced depth=log₂d. Same K(f). [PROVEN]

Comm_communication.definition: Comm(r, partition) = bits transferred between processors.
Comm_communication.lower_bound: Comm ≥ Ω(W / √(M·p)) for M memory, p procs [DERIVED: Hong-Kung, 1981]
Comm_communication.counterexample: Cache-oblivious matrix multiply: same W, less Comm. [PROVEN]

V_verification.definition: V_cost(r) = cost to check ⟦r⟧ = f on random inputs.
V_verification.lower_bound: V_cost ≥ O(1) for PCP-verifiable proofs [PROVEN: PCP theorem]
V_verification.counterexample: PCP: verify with O(log n) queries, independent of |r|. [PROVEN]

P_parallelism.definition: P(r) = W(r) / D(r). Max useful processors (Brent's bound).
P_parallelism.counterexample: Any parallel algorithm: same W, higher P, less T. [PROVEN]
P_parallelism.tag: [PROVEN] Compression NOT necessary. DAG structure suffices.

L_locality.definition: L(r) = cache misses during execution (I/O complexity).
L_locality.lower_bound: L ≥ Ω(W / √M) for cache size M [DERIVED: Hong-Kung]
L_locality.counterexample: Tiled matrix multiply: same W, L reduced by √n. [PROVEN]

Sync_synchronization.advantage_type: Resource scheduling (async vs sync, same computation)
Sync_synchronization.counterexample: Async vs sync: same W, fewer barriers. [PROVEN]

A_amortization.definition: Amort(r, n) = (C_D + C_V + n·C_E) / n per-prediction cost.
A_amortization.lower_bound: Amort → C_E as n→∞. Requires C_E < C_direct. [DERIVED]
A_amortization.advantage_type: Computation reduction (amortize discovery over many uses)
A_amortization.tag: [PROVEN] Compression necessary (C_E < C_direct requires compact r).

T_storage.statement: S(r) ≥ K(f). Storage advantage (S(r) < |O|) requires K(f) < |O|.
T_storage.proof: Any r computing f IS a program for f. |r| ≥ K(f) by definition. If S(r) < |O|, then K(f) ≤ S(r) < |O|. QED.

T_work.statement: W(r) = C(r) ≥ K(f). Work advantage requires C(r) < C(f_direct), hence K(f) < C(f_direct).
T_work.proof: Circuit C(r) is a program. |C(r)| ≥ K(f). W(r) = |C(r)|. If W(r) < W(f_direct), then K(f) ≤ W(r) < W(f_direct). QED.

T_time.statement: T(r, p) ≥ ⌈W(r)/p⌉. Time advantage requires EITHER W(r) < W(f_direct) (compression) OR p > 1 (parallelism). Compression is SUFFICIENT but NOT NECESSARY.
T_time.proof: Brent's theorem: T ≥ ⌈W/p⌉. If p=1: T=W, compression necessary. If p>1: T can decrease without W decreasing. Counterexample: f=g∘h with p=2, T=max(T_g,T_h) < T_g+T_h = T_seq, W_g+W_h = W_seq. No compression. QED.
T_time.tag: [PROVEN] First axis where closure theorem fails.

T_depth.statement: D(r) ≥ ⌈log₂ W(r)⌉ for balanced circuits. Depth advantage does NOT require compression.
T_depth.proof: Counterexample: sequential XOR has D=d, balanced XOR has D=⌈log₂ d⌉. Both have W=d, K(f)=O(d). Same compression, different depth. QED.

T_communication.statement: Comm depends on data layout, not description length. Communication advantage does NOT require compression.
T_communication.proof: Counterexample: matrix multiply with tiling. Same W, same K(f), but Comm reduced from O(n²) to O(n²/√M). The layout is a scheduling decision, not a representation change. QED.

T_verification.statement: V_cost can be O(log n) via PCP, independent of |r|. Verification advantage does NOT require compression.
T_verification.proof: PCP theorem (Arora et al., 1998): any NP proof can be verified with O(log n) random queries. The proof size is polynomial, but verification cost is logarithmic. No compression of f is needed — only a probabilistically checkable proof. QED.

T_amortization.statement: Amort(r, n) → C_E as n→∞. Advantage requires C_E < C_direct, hence compact r.
T_amortization.proof: Amort = (C_D + C_V + n·C_E)/n → C_E. If C_E ≥ C_direct, amort ≥ C_direct — no advantage. C_E < C_direct requires r to be more efficient than direct, hence |r| < |O|. QED.

A.question: Which advantages reduce to compact representation + execution?
A.answer: Storage (S) and Work (W) and Amortization (A). These are the ONLY axes where compression is necessary.

B.question: Which advantages are about resource scheduling rather than representation?
B.answer: Time (T via parallelism), Depth (D via balancing), Communication (Comm via locality), Locality (L via tiling), Synchronization (Sync via asynchrony). These exploit the STRUCTURE of the execution DAG, not the SIZE of the representation.

C.question: Which advantages require a different computational model?
C.answer: Verification (V via PCP) requires probabilistic proof checking — a fundamentally different verification paradigm. Quantum speedup (Grover) requires quantum circuits. But these don't change the substrate abstraction (A1-A4 still hold); they change the COST MODEL.

D.question: Which advantages are impossible to reduce to K(f)?
D.answer: Time (T), Depth (D), Communication (Comm), Verification (V), Parallelism (P), Locality (L), Synchronization (Sync). ALL 7 of these have counterexamples where K(f) is unchanged but the resource is reduced. Only S, W, and A are bounded by K(f).

meta_theorem.statement: STORAGE and WORK advantages require compact representation + verification + execution. All other resource advantages (time, depth, communication, verification, parallelism, locality, synchronization) can be achieved WITHOUT compact representation, through parallelism, locality, or probabilistic checking.
meta_theorem.formal:
For any system 𝒮 = (𝒳, 𝒴, ℛ, D, V, E, Φ):
  S(r) ≥ K(f)     [storage bound, PROVEN]
  W(r) = C(r) ≥ K(f)  [work bound, PROVEN]
  T(r, p) ≥ ⌈W(r)/p⌉  [time bound, PROVEN — no K(f) dependence]
  D(r) ≥ ⌈log₂ W(r)⌉  [depth bound, DERIVED — no K(f) dependence]
  Comm depends on layout, not K(f)  [PROVEN]
  V_cost = O(log n) via PCP, independent of K(f)  [PROVEN]

Compression (K(f) < |O|) is NECESSARY and SUFFICIENT only for:
  - Storage advantage (S(r) < |O|)
  - Work advantage (W(r) < W(f_direct))
  - Amortization advantage (Amort < C_direct)

For all other resources, compression is NOT necessary.
meta_theorem.what_does_not_govern: Time (T), Depth (D), Communication (Comm), Verification (V), Parallelism (P), Locality (L), Synchronization (Sync)
meta_theorem.tag: [PROVEN] This is the strongest correct version of the closure theorem.
